settings.title: Build on your school with *code or an AI assistant*
settings.description: CourseLit has a REST API for your own code and an MCP server for assistants. Both run on the same service, use the same credentials and expose the same operations.
settings.smallPrint: API keys, the REST API and MCP are on every plan.

settings.code:
curl -X POST "https://api.courselit.app/v1/products" \
  -H "x-api-key: $COURSELIT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "kind": "course",
    "title": "Intro to watercolor",
    "description": "Learn the basics of painting with watercolor."
  }'
settings.caption: Create a draft course with one request. New products are always drafts.

settings.title: Make your first call in three steps

items.title: Create an API key
items.description: The school owner opens Settings, then API keys, names the key and picks only the permissions it needs.

items.title: Send it in a header
items.description: Pass the key in the x-api-key header. A key belongs to one school, so no other setup is needed.

items.title: Call any operation
items.description: Every operation sits under /v1. Requests and responses are JSON.

settings.title: Let an AI assistant run your school
settings.body:
CourseLit runs a remote MCP server. Add its address as a connector in **Claude**, **ChatGPT** or **Cursor**, sign in with CourseLit, and the assistant can build courses, set up pricing, grant learner access and edit your website.

There is one named, typed tool for each REST operation, such as `list_sections`. Tools that delete data, publish, email contacts or change payment or access settings need an explicit confirmation.

[Read the MCP guide](/docs/developers/mcp-server)

settings.code: Set up my first offer in CourseLit. Follow https://courselit.app/docs/setup.md
settings.caption: Set up your first offer: paste this into your assistant. It interviews you, builds a draft and asks before publishing.

settings.title: Credentials and permissions you can reason about
settings.description: REST and MCP share one set of rules, so a permission means the same thing everywhere.

items.title: School API keys
items.description: A key belongs to the school, not a person, and never has more access than the permissions you gave it. Keys can expire, and you can revoke one at any time.

items.title: OAuth for assistants
items.description: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE. The token carries the permissions the person has in the school, narrowed to the scopes they approved.

items.title: Cursor pagination
items.description: Most lists return items and a nextCursor, with 1 to 50 items per page. Contacts and customers use page numbers and return a total.

items.title: Clear errors and limits
items.description: Errors share one JSON shape with a stable code. The default limit is 1,200 requests per minute per address, and a 429 includes Retry-After.

settings.title: What is not available yet
settings.body:
CourseLit does **not** send outgoing webhooks to your own endpoints, and the API does not support idempotency keys. To react to changes, read the data with the API on a schedule.

CourseLit does receive webhooks from the payment provider each school connects. That is handled for you.

[Webhooks and events](/docs/developers/webhooks) · [Rate limits and retries](/docs/developers/rate-limits-and-retries)

items.question: Do I need a paid plan to use the API?
items.answer: No. API keys, the REST API and the MCP server are available on every plan. Self-hosted CourseLit includes them too.

items.question: Can an API key do everything?
items.answer: No. Operations that move money, change who can sign in or run code on the learner site are limited to signed-in people. The reference shows what each operation accepts.

items.question: Which assistants work with the MCP server?
items.answer: Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor connect with OAuth. Any other client that supports remote MCP servers can connect with the server address, or with an API key if it cannot complete a browser sign-in.

items.question: Can an assistant publish or delete things by itself?
items.answer: Not without you. Deleting, publishing, emailing contacts and changing payment or access settings need an explicit confirmation, and the assistant is expected to ask first.

items.question: Is there an API for self-hosted CourseLit?
items.answer: Yes. The base URL is the PUBLIC_API_URL your operator configured. Hosted CourseLit uses https://api.courselit.app.
